title: SLO-aware speculative executor for mixed-quant inference
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and ship a runtime executor that speculatively attempts lower-precision (FP8/INT8) kernels first while remaining SLO-aware and able to fallback to FP16. Goal: reduce token cost and average latency for typical workloads without violating per-tenant latency SLOs or causing unacceptable accuracy regressions. The executor must use lightweight per-request predictors + a micro-calibration sampler to validate accuracy online and drive safe fallbacks.
proposal:
1) Introduce a per-request decision layer that combines: predicted latency delta, estimated accuracy delta (from a small learned estimator), and tenant SLO budget to choose an initial precision path (FP8-first, INT8-first, or FP16).
2) Implement a speculative execution mode: dispatch the smallest-latency kernel (typically FP8 quantized) and concurrently start a shadow FP16 execution for a sampled subset of requests (sample rate configurable by tenant). Shadow runs feed an online accuracy reservoir used to update the estimator.
3) If the estimator or shadow validation indicates accuracy drift beyond thresholds, automatically switch that tenant's routing policy to a safer path (e.g., FP16 or hybrid per-layer routing).
4) Integrate with autoscaling & admission control: if tail latency approaches SLO, throttle FP8 speculative paths and bump to more conservative kernels to preserve tail.
5) Expose per-tenant telemetry + dashboard with accuracy deltas, decision histogram, and cost savings so PMs and SREs can audit behavior.
acceptance_criteria: E2E canary rollout completes with no customer-facing errors on dedicated test tenants
Average token cost reduced by >= 12% for the benchmarked NLU workload (compare default FP16 baseline)
90th-percentile latency across mixed workloads remains within tenant SLOs (no more than 5% violations relative to baseline)
Online shadow validation shows accuracy regression <= 0.5% on high-sensitivity prompt set; any drift triggers automatic conservative routing
Telemetry surfaces decision-level attribution (why FP8 chosen) and is queryable per-tenant and per-model
Automated integration tests that simulate quantization-induced failure modes (out-of-distribution prompts, long context) are green

comments: 2026-02-28 | Aisha Patel: Initial triage - flagged as P0 because this unlocks cost savings for multiple large tenants. Created proposal and listed immediate risks (accuracy regressions, tail-latency amplification).

2026-03-03 | Marco Ruiz: Prototype estimator shows ~70% precision at predicting per-request accuracy delta using a 128-d embedding distance feature + prompt metadata. Need wider sample to reduce false positives for rare prompts.

2026-03-06 | Reliability (N. Chen): Identified an infra constraint: speculative shadow runs double GPU memory if not carefully scheduled. Recommend implementing sampled shadow on a separate low-priority pool to avoid eviction of primary work.

2026-03-09 | Observability (R. Gomez): Telemetry schema v2 submitted in PR #6482; decision event includes reason, estimator_score, selected_path, fallback_count. Confirmed retention 90 days for raw metrics.

2026-03-12 | Marco Ruiz: Integration smoke tests show 12.7% cost reduction on NLU benchmark with 1% shadow sampling; 90p latency stayed within SLO on synthetic traffic. Edge case: very long contexts (>8k tokens) produced higher fallback rate — adding per-length gating.
2026-03-14 | Aisha Patel: Design review scheduled for 2026-03-18. Next steps: finalize thresholds, add adaptive sampling to reduce shadow cost, and draft canary rollout playbook.
